title: Bromide displaces chloride from chloromethane, drawn with two arrows that are individually chemically impossible but whose aggregate per atom and per bond declared deltas equal the correct mechanism's

expect.note: ADVERSARIAL FINDING, not a normal good fixture, kept in the corpus deliberately as a documented gap rather than fixed, because fixing it means writing an arrow legality check and this pass may not do that. CLAUDE.md names 'arrow legality' as one of the four things chem-core is responsible for, alongside valence, mass, and charge and electron bookkeeping. No function in chem-core and no check in this validator package currently asserts it: nothing requires an ElectronSource and its ElectronSink to be physically adjacent, meaning bonded to each other or to a common atom, before the pair is accepted as one arrow. This fixture is the correct SN2 substrate and product from good-sn2-with-spectator-counterion, with the two mechanistically correct arrows replaced by two different, individually nonsensical arrows: arrow a1 sources the breaking C-Cl bond directly into the forming C-Br bond, which draws the leaving group's own bonding pair becoming the incoming nucleophile's bond, rather than the nucleophile donating its own lone pair; arrow a2 sources bromide's lone pair and sinks it as a lone pair landing on chloride directly, which requires the electrons to cross a bond that does not exist between two atoms that are never adjacent in this species graph, Br1 and Cl1 are never bonded to each other at any point in the step. Neither arrow is one a chemistry teacher would accept. But declaredDeltas only accumulates a running total keyed by atom id and by unordered atom pair, and the two wrong arrows here were chosen so that their combined declared total, Br1 nonbonding -2, Cl1 nonbonding +2, bond(C1,Br1) +2, bond(C1,Cl1) -2, is bit for bit identical to what the correct pair of arrows declares. conservation-electron-flow compares only that aggregate against observedDeltas and cannot tell the two mechanisms apart, so it reports zero violations, and no other check in this family looks at arrows at all. The suite reports this fixture as fully valid chemistry. It is not. This is reported as a finding rather than encoded as a broken fixture with mustFail, because there is no check name in CONSERVATION_CHECK_NAMES this package could declare as the one that is supposed to catch it; the gap is the absence of a seventh check, not a bug in one of the six that exist.
